title: Private deployments: VPC & on-prem requirements, reference architectures, day-2 ops, upgrade & rollback
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended deployment requirements, reference architectures, on-prem packaging guidance, day-2 operations checklist, and standard upgrade/rollback procedures for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for platform engineers, customer SREs, and solutions engineers executing a private deployment or supporting day-to-day operations.

Scope

- VPC-based private deployments (public cloud private account + VPC peering, PrivateLink)
- On-prem / air-gapped package deployments (k8s, bare metal Rack + GPU nodes)
- Day-2 operations: monitoring, scaling, backups, incident response
- Upgrade and rollback process for platform components and model-serving images
- Customer requirements mapping (networking, compliance, capacity)

Ownership and Contacts

- Owner team: engineering (eng-private-deployments)
- Primary owner: Ava Chen (Platform PM)
- Oncall escalation: private-deployments-sre@redwood.ai
- Recommended reviewers for custom deployments: solutions-engineering, security-compliance

High-level Architecture (reference)

1) VPC deployment (cloud):
   - Components: private-control-plane (managed by Redwood), redwood-private-operator (customer VPC), inference-gateway (NLB), model-store (S3 compatible or cloud storage), metrics/observability (Prometheus pushgateway relay), audit-logging agent
   - Network layout: 3 AZs, 2 subnets per AZ (worker / management), NAT gateway in management subnets for image pulls (or use private ECR/access endpoints)

2) On-prem deployment (air-gapped option):
   - Components: redwood-operator, inference-gateway (LB or vip), model-store (minio or local object store), hardware pool (GPU nodes), local monitoring cluster (Prometheus + Grafana), kafka for async job queues (optional)
   - Packaging: OCI images distributed via pre-authorized registry or tarball + manifests + helm charts

Predeployment Requirements (Checklist)

Networking & Security
- VPC CIDR recommendation: 10.200.0.0/16 (adjust to avoid overlap).
- Subnet layout: public subnet for bastion (optional), private subnets for control-plane (10.200.32.0/19) and worker GPU nodes (10.200.64.0/18) across AZs.
- Required ports: 443 (api), 22 (admin - restricted), 9100/9101 (node exporters - internal), 9090 (Prometheus - internal), 2379 (etcd if self-hosted - internal).
- Security groups / firewall rules: restrict control-plane to customer admin CIDRs and Redwood management CIDRs (if using managed control plane).
- Private image registry: customer-provided or Redwood-hosted pull endpoint via PrivateLink / VPC peering.

Identity & Access
- IAM roles: allow kube node role to read images from registry and access object store.
- KMS/HSM: recommended for LLK (model encryption) keys; integrate with customer KMS for private deployments.
- RBAC: create platform-admin, platform-operator, read-only roles.

Compute & Storage
- GPU types supported: NVIDIA A100 (preferred), H100, RTX6000 for smaller customers. Specify CUDA driver compatibility.
- Node sizing: min 4 GPU nodes (prod small) each with 80Gi root + 1Ti model cache disk.
- Persistent volumes: use high-throughput NVMe for model cache; MinIO/ceph for object store.

Operational Requirements
- Time sync (NTP), LDAP/AD integration (optional), certificate authority (internal or customer CA)
- Backup location: offsite object storage with 90-day retention for critical configs and helm release backups

Reference Architecture Diagrams (textual)

- VPC (3 AZ): [bastion] -> [management subnets: control-plane components (operator, etcd)] -> [worker subnets: inference pods with GPU] -> [NLB inference-gateway] -> internet via NAT only for image pulls (or none for fully air-gapped).
- On-prem rack: management switch -> control-plane servers -> GPU racks -> local object-store -> edge load balancer -> customer network.

Packaging & Distribution

1) Cloud (VPC):
   - Standard distribution uses Helm charts + image manifest with tag immutability.
   - Registry access via PrivateLink or IAM role-based ECR access.

2) Air-gapped / On-Prem:
   - Deliverables: signed OCI image bundle (tar.gz), helm charts (versioned), kubectl/helm manifests, install script, SHA256 checksums, install guide.
   - Installation path: unpack images -> load into local registry -> helm install redwood-operator --namespace redwood-system --set imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent
   - Required customer steps: provide reachable registry endpoint, provide KMS credentials (if used), confirm network and DNS resolution in cluster.

Day-2 Operations (Runbook Summaries)

1) Routine health checks (daily):
   - Verify cluster node health (kubectl get nodes).
   - Verify inference-gateway p95/p99 latency < 200ms for internal smoke tests.
   - Confirm Prometheus alert count == 0 for critical alerts.

2) Scaling GPUs (procedure):
   - Evaluate load: check pod CPU/GPU utilization (nvidia-smi metrics + kube-metrics).
   - Add new GPU nodes to the autoscaling group (cloud) or power-on additional rack nodes (on-prem).
   - Ensure nodes join cluster and taints/labels applied: kubectl label nodes <node> rwi/gpu=true
   - Trigger rolling restart for operator-managed deployments to pick up new capacity: kubectl rollout restart deployment/redwood-operator -n redwood-system

3) Node replacement (failed GPU node):
   - Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
   - Drain node excluding pods with local storage: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
   - Replace hardware or reprovision instance; after ready, uncordon.

4) Certificate rotation (annual or compromise):
   - Generate new certs via customer CA or Redwood tool; update secrets in redwood-system: kubectl create secret tls rwi-tls --cert=cert.pem --key=key.pem -n redwood-system
   - Restart ingress/inference-gateway pods.

Upgrade and Rollback Procedures

Goals: safe, reversible upgrades with minimal impact to serving availability. Follow a staged canary approach for all platform and model-serving components.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Back up current Helm releases: helm get values redwood-operator -n redwood-system > /backups/redwood-operator-values-$(date +%F).yaml
- Snapshot etcd (if self-hosted) and cluster state
- Ensure runbook and rollback owner oncall assigned
- Confirm smoke tests and release candidate image SHA512 checksum

Staged upgrade procedure (recommended):
1) Canary (5% capacity)
   - Deploy new operator / image to a canary node pool labeled rwi/canary=true with limited capacity (5% of traffic).
   - Run smoke tests: inference correctness (sample prompts), throughput validation, latency p95/p99 comparison.
   - Acceptance criteria: error rate delta < 0.5pp, p99 latency increase < 10%, CPU/GPU memory within expected bounds.
2) Gradual rollout
   - If canary passes, incrementally increase percentage (20% -> 50% -> 100%) using traffic routing or by moving workloads between node pools.
   - Monitor key metrics for 30-60 minutes at each step.
3) Full rollout
   - Update Helm chart and annotate release: helm upgrade redwood-operator ./charts/redwood-operator -n redwood-system --set image.tag=<new-tag>

Rollback procedure (if acceptance criteria fail):
- Immediately pause rollout and divert traffic to previous node pool (if traffic-splitting configured).
- Revert Helm release: helm rollback redwood-operator <previous-release-number> -n redwood-system
- If helm rollback not possible, re-deploy from backup manifests: kubectl apply -f /backups/redwood-operator-values-<date>.yaml
- Post-rollback: run full smoke tests and create an incident ticket with triage notes.

Automated tests and smoke checks (minimum):
- API: /v1/health, /v1/generate smoke calls with canned prompts
- Model correctness: token-level checksum comparison for deterministic prompts (where applicable)
- Metrics: error rate < 1% for smoke tests, p95/p99 latency within threshold

Customer Requirements Library (table)

This table lists common customer requirements and the recommended Redwood response/integration pattern.

Requirement | Typical customer ask | Redwood recommended configuration
--- | --- | ---
Network isolation | PrivateLink or VPC-peering only, no public IPs | Deploy control plane via PrivateLink; use NAT for image pulls or provide registry mirror
Data residency | Data must stay in customer region | Deploy Private control plane inside customer VPC; store telemetry in customer-managed buckets
Key management | Customer KMS required for model keys | Integrate with customer KMS/HSM; store key references in Secrets Manager
Audit logging | 365-day immutable logs | Enable audit-log-forwarder to customer S3/GCS with lifecycle policy
Air-gapped installs | No outbound internet allowed | OCI image bundle + local registry + manual helm install + offline verification checklist
GPU compliance | Specific GPU vendors/certifications | Validate driver versions and provide vendor compatibility matrix; recommend A100/H100 with specified CUDA

Checklist: Additional customer-specific info to collect before engagement
- Expected QPS and model size(s) (tokens/sec + model weights GB)
- Required retention for logs and eval traces
- Compliance requirements: SOC2, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI (if applicable)
- Preferred maintenance windows and change control process

Runbooks and Playbooks (links and embedded snippets)

- Incident: inference degradation (p95 spike)
  1) Identify affected services: kubectl get pods -A | grep inference
  2) Check metrics: prometheus query for rwi_inference_latency_seconds{quantile=\"0.99\"}
  3) If deployment-level issue, rollback to previous stable release per rollback procedure

- Incident: model cache corruption
  1) Quarantine affected nodes (cordon)
  2) Evict pods and clear model cache directory on node: rm -rf /var/lib/rwi/model-cache/*
  3) Re-sync models from object-store via admin job: kubectl create job sync-models --image=redwood-admin:stable -n redwood-admin

Appendix: commands and config snippets

Example Helm upgrade:
helm upgrade redwood-operator ./charts/redwood-operator -n redwood-system --set image.tag=2026.06.01-rc --atomic --timeout 15m

Example canary node labeling:
kubectl label node ip-10-200-64-12 rwi/canary=true

Prometheus alert thresholds (recommended):
- rwi_inference_error_rate > 0.01 for 5m -> P1
- rwi_inference_p99_latency > baseline*1.25 for 5m -> P1
